Hossein Estiri's research spans computational phenomics, environmental health informatics, temporal machine learning, and agentic AI for clinical decision support.

In the Confluence Projects, he co-developed GridEX with Chirag Patel and leads the work that links environmental exposure to longitudinal health records: identifying dementia and its precursors in clinical data, and measuring how fully and how quickly older adults recover after illness. He is contact principal investigator of the NIA-funded R01AG096492 on dementia and the environmental exposome, and a principal investigator of the NIMHD-funded Community CATALYST Center with OCHIN.

He has led multi-site AI studies in the ENACT and PCORnet networks, and his work has twice been selected as a best paper in clinical research informatics by the IMIA Yearbook of Medical Informatics.
